title: Console Walkthrough: Usage Analytics & Per-Route Cost Breakdown - Arcadia Retail
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood PM), Lina (Arcadia CTO), Marco (Arcadia Eng Mgr), Rebecca (Arcadia SRE), Tom (Arcadia PM)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: Quick Console walkthrough focused on per-route dashboards, usage analytics, and explicit cost breakdowns for API + embedding traffic. Customer is evaluating sending user-facing chat + background embeddings; main concerns are cost per 1M tokens, per-route spikes, and VPC/Private deployment options for PII.
Topics: [Console overview, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown methodology, retention and audit logs, routing & fallback, benchmarking/pilot next steps]

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. this is Alex from Redwood, im the AE here and with me is Samir our solutions eng. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lina: hey thanks, doing well. we're excited to see the console stuff actually.
[00:11] Marco: yeah, we got a lot of questions on cost and the per-route stuff.
[00:15] Samir: perfect; quick agenda — i'll start with the usage analytics view then show per-route dashboards and how to break down token and embedding spend, then priya will touch on recommended optimize settings.
[00:25] Marco: sounds good.
[00:30] Samir: okay jumping in — this is the main usage analytics page, you can see total tokens, request rate, p50/p95 latency by model. excuse the transcript, console sometimes shows as "Redwood Consolee" on my screen — ignore that, but main metrics are here.
[00:45] [00:45] Samir: so route A which is our customer chat api, you can filter by model, time window — here we have token volume, average tokens per request, and request count. you can also stack by environment - prod/stage — real-time streaming updates.
[01:05] Rebecca: can you show where we get the cost numbers? is that computed or do we upload our own cost?
[01:11] Samir: good question. cost is computed from our unit price profile (hosted MSRP or your contract rates) combined with per-model unit consumption. by default it shows an estimated cost using Redwood hosted pricing, but if you connect your contract/commit details or dedicated pricing it will use that. the per-route view breaks down model cost vs infra adjustments (like quantized variants).
[01:30] Lina: does that include embeddings? our search team runs a lot of background embeddings and that's the big bill right now.
[01:36] Samir: yes. embeddings are shown as a separate "embedding" metric with vectors per second and token-equivalent cost. note that embedding costs are normalized to a token-equivalent for the cost UI because some customers prefer comparing them side-by-side. franky sometimes that creates confusion, so we add a tooltip.
[01:55] Marco: what about per-user or per-tenant breakdown? we need to charge our business units.
[02:01] Samir: you can tag routes and keys with tenant ids; per-route and per-api-key dashboards will then show that split. we also have exported CSV/BigQuery for downstream billing.
[02:15] [02:15] Samir: switching to the per-route dashboard — here's route A, you can see a waterfall: tokens, model selection (gpt-like vs small open model), batching efficiency, and cache hit rate. note the KV cache label is sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash" in older docs, but this UI shows prefix KV-caching hit rate.
[02:38] Tom: explain batching efficiency a bit more — we run many short queries, how do we avoid latency regressions?
[02:44] Samir: good point. batching is workload-aware: the Optimize engine suggests batch windows and max batch sizes per route to strike a balance. for short queries we recommend smaller max-batch but enable continuous batching; in console you can simulate the expected p95 impact before applying.
[03:05] Alex: i'll jump in with cost breakdown example — hypothetically for 1M tokens on model X it's $X in model compute plus $Y infra premium; the console shows token units and overlays estimated cost.
[03:18] [03:18] Marco: how do you treat streaming vs non-streaming? streaming users often pay the same model tokens but see different latency patterns.
[03:25] Samir: it's the same token accounting; streaming doesn't change token price but affects compute time and latency SLOs; the console segregates streaming traffic so you can see the different latency curves.
[03:40] Rebecca: security — we need audit logs and SSO. can you show the retention and logs area?
[03:47] Priya: sure. under Settings -> Security you can see audit logs, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. logs can be retained per route for up to 7 years under enterprise retention add-on.
[04:05] Lina: is SOC 2 covered? and what about data residency EU?
[04:09] Priya: yes SOC 2 Type II, ISO is in progress, and we have EU regions; for strict residency we recommend Private (VPC) deployment or Dedicated with region pinning.
[04:22] [04:22] Marco: if we do Dedicated, do we still get these per-route analytics?
[04:26] Samir: yes, the same console surfaces Dedicated and Private metrics; for Private there's an agent that ships metrics while respecting customer network controls. there might be an on-prem forwarding agent if air-gapped, small caveat is retention depending on your storage.
[04:45] Lina: ok show a concrete example of cost hot spots — please show last 7 days.
[04:50] Samir: here — you can see spikes on route B coinciding with a quantized model fallback. hover shows requests where model fallback occurred due to capacity; console marks these as fallbacks and provides counts.
[05:05] Alex: that's an important devops signal — if fallbacks cause higher latency or higher cost, you can create a reroute policy to prefer a cheaper model variant when tokens per request exceed threshold.
[05:18] Marco: what about volume discounts / reserved capacity?
[05:21] Priya: reserved capacity (Dedicated) shows committed vs actual usage; the console projects burn-rate against commit and alerts if you're approaching limits. for cost calc we apply commit discounts in the per-route cost model when you attach your contract id.
[05:40] Rebecca: any integration with our billing system? we use Stripe + internal billing.
[05:45] Samir: we export usage to BigQuery/CSV and can provide a webhooks-fed billing export; some customers map route-level metrics to internal chargeback keys.
[05:58] Lina: can we run a pilot with our real traffic and run the Console analytics for two weeks?
[06:03] Alex: yes, typically we do a short pilot — we'll need api keys, a small dataset, and a test plan. we'll also run a cheap benchmark to estimate cost per 1M tokens under typical mix.
[06:18] Marco: what about PII? embedding payloads contain user addresses; we need redaction options.
[06:24] Priya: we support client-side redaction and server-side field-level masking; for Private you can bring your own redaction pipeline. also KMS ensures customer keys for encryption-at-rest.
[06:38] [06:38] Samir: quick note on Optimize recommendations — console surfaces suggestions: enable selective caching on certain prefixes, recommend quantized model variant (8-bit) for background embeddings, and recommended batch sizes per route. you can apply suggestions or schedule them as experiments (canary rollout).
[06:58] Marco: show the canary UI for a rollout?
[07:02] Samir: sure, this is the rollout screen — pick percentage, route, and metrics to monitor; it will auto rollback if error or latency thresholds breached.
[07:17] Alex: okay we are about 40 minutes in — any other security or procurement concerns?
[07:22] Lina: procurement wants terms on data retention and indemnity; we also need a vendor security pack.
[07:28] Alex: we'll share our security pack and a tenancy docs; i'll follow up.
[07:32] Tom: and pricing; can you show a sample quote?
[07:36] Alex: we'll send a tailored pricing deck — estimate included for the pilot and projected monthly at scale.
[07:42] Marco: any mentions of competitors? we evaluated OpenAI endpoints and Anthropic internally.
[07:48] Samir: console has built-in comparator charts but we avoid publishing third-party prices; we can help run a benchmark against their endpoints if useful.
[07:59] [07:59] Rebecca: few minor QA quips — the transcription on the demo recording sometimes mangles SAML as "samel", ignore that.
[08:06] Alex: noted. last bits: next steps and action items.
[08:12] Alex: recap — we'll send: 1) pricing deck + pilot proposal 2) security pack + SOC2 report 3) instructions to spin up test api keys + sample dataset 4) propose pilot start date next Tue.
[08:28] Lina: good, thanks.
[08:32] Marco: thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
